entries.title: Football evolves through rule, personnel and strategic interaction
entries.summary: Football strategy changes as rules, player specialization, substitution, passing rules, roster construction and opposing innovations change. Historical concepts must be interpreted in their era before applying them to modern football.
principles: Do not assume historical statistical environments are directly comparable.
limitations: Historical attribution can be contested; provenance should preserve competing accounts.
fantasyImplications: Historical knowledge primarily improves causal/schematic understanding; direct fantasy application requires modern evidence.

provenance.note: Program-level historical principle; detailed sourced timeline pending.

entries.title: Systems evolve through coaching lineages and adaptation
entries.summary: Named offensive and defensive systems are families of ideas that evolve as coaches teach, combine and adapt concepts; labels should not be treated as immutable playbooks.
principles: Track coach-to-coach influence separately from current observed tendency.
Record concepts inherited, changed or abandoned.
limitations: Coaching-tree membership does not prove a current team uses a particular concept at a particular rate.
fantasyImplications: Lineage can generate hypotheses about role and scheme, but current usage evidence must dominate.

provenance.note: Historical/coaching graph principle; named lineages to be sourced individually.

entries.title: Coryell system study node
entries.summary: Create a sourced study of Don Coryell's offensive philosophy, historical development, terminology/concepts, coaching influence, defensive responses and modern descendants. No specific schematic claim is promoted until sourced.
principles: Separate contemporary primary evidence from later summaries.
Map concepts and descendants rather than reducing the system to a single label such as vertical passing.
limitations: Air Coryell is often used loosely; system-specific claims require sourcing and era context.
fantasyImplications: Potential historical foundation for understanding modern vertical spacing and role concepts; fantasy use requires current-team evidence and validation.

provenance.note: Prioritized because it connects historical study, modern scheme lineage and first-hand user experience.
